thread:
maya: Heads-up — after rolling runtime v2.14.0 to the canary cohort (~5% traffic) we're seeing p95 jump ~220ms on text-gen endpoints for several tenants. Noticed ~20:05 UTC.
ajay: saw alerts too. Is it across all kernels or specific ones?
devon: quick check: most traffic hitting kernel-v3 (quant path). p50 stable, p95/p99 up. linked dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/abc123
samir: any auth or quota errors in logs? could be retries inflating tail.
maya: no 5xx spike, no auth failures. request counts normal. traces show a subset of requests with long scheduling wait before gpu exec.
triage-bot: detected p95 delta +210ms vs baseline for route /v1/generate for cohort canary-2026-03-16. Related alerts channel: #incidents
ajay: paste sample span timeline? a couple of traces would help.
maya: example trace snippet:
```
span scheduling_wait 198ms
span kernel_start 2ms
span gpu_exec 12ms
span kv_cache_miss 0ms
```
(weirdly scheduling_wait is the culprit)
devon: scheduling wait suggests queuing at the runtime scheduler or tenant scheduler mis-accounting. Did the rollout include scheduler change or new prefetch config?
maya: rollout diff shows runtime: bump default max-inflight from 100 -> 80 for better fairness. That was intended to reduce OOM risk.
samir: lowering max-inflight can increase latency for bursty cohorts. Canary traffic shape might be burstier than baseline sample.
ajay: can we verify inflight counts on affected hosts? query:
```
sum by(host) (runtime_inflight_requests{env=prod,cohort="canary-2026-03-16"})
```
maya: running now — attaching top host snippet:
```
host-a: 78
host-b: 77
host-c: 79
```
we're hitting the new cap.
devon: suggests we throttled concurrency. Quick mitigation options:
- roll runtime config back to max-inflight=100 for canary
- increase pool size for canary cohort
- apply temporary routing split to move high-burst tenants off canary
maya: support-ops, which customers are impacted? any escalations?
support-ops: two customers filed latency complaints (acme-inc, shoply). Both within the canary cohort. No billing issues reported.
ajay: for investigation we should bisect whether the change to max-inflight is sole cause. Plan:
1) Reproduce locally with synthetic burst to canary config. (devon)
2) Temporarily flip canary config to old concurrency on a subset of hosts (maya)
3) If mitigates, rollback config for canary while keeping rollout paused (samir)
4) Run synthetic replay to measure p95/p99 with/without the cap (devon)

devon: repro command for replay tool:
```
replay --cohort canary-2026-03-16 --qps 1500 --burst 300 --model redwood-3b --duration 5m
```
maya: I'm going to patch canary hosts az-east-1-host-{a,b} to max-inflight=100 and watch.
triage-bot: deploy change planned by maya at 20:40 UTC. Auto-notify on metric delta.

(20:43 UTC)
maya: patched host-a,b -> p95 on route dropped ~180ms, p99 dropped ~320ms on those hosts. overall canary p95 dropped ~100ms.
ajay: that points to concurrency cap being the main driver. Are there any reasons we reduced cap initially? release notes mentioned fairness improvements for cold-start heavy workloads.
samir: fairness is fine but the default was too low for certain burst patterns. We need workload-aware default or autoscaling of inflight cap.
devon: proposed follow-ups:
- revert default in v2.14.0 to previous value (100) and re-run canary with monitoring
- add a rollout gate: if p95 delta > 50ms for any active cohort, hold and alert
- add sampling instrumentation to surface per-tenant burstiness during canary

maya: I'll open a PR to revert the default and add the gate. tagging: @ajay for rollback approval, @devon for repro results in the PR.
support-ops: I'll reach out to the two customers with proactive note: "we're aware of transient latency in canary cohort; mitigation in flight; no action required on your side" :email:
ajay: once PR merges, coordinate quick canary re-deploy and monitor for 30m before resuming rollout.
devon: also recommend a temporary tweak: increase scheduler backoff and allow short burst tokens for bursty tenants.
maya: action items summary:
- maya: open PR to revert max-inflight default + add rollout gate (in progress)
- devon: run replay baseline vs cap and upload results to PR (in progress)
- samir: prepare rollback plan for full rollout if canary rollback doesn't restore metrics (standby)
- support-ops: notify impacted customers (sent)

samir: one more note — add a dashboard panel for inflight vs p95 to make root cause correlations easier in future.
maya: agreed. will add to postmortem/triage notes.
ajay: great triage, keep this thread updated with PR link and replay results.
maya: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/infra/changes/4587 — posting replay results in a few mins. :thumbsup:
